name: Prompt Injection
paraphrase: Crafted direct or indirect input (user text, retrieved documents, tool output) changes the model's behaviour against the designer's intent.

name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
paraphrase: The model or the system around it reveals personal, confidential or proprietary data in its output.

name: Supply Chain
paraphrase: Third-party models, adapters, libraries, tools or datasets introduce vulnerabilities or tampered components.

name: Data and Model Poisoning
paraphrase: Training, fine-tuning or embedding data is manipulated to plant bias, backdoors or wrong behaviour.

name: Improper Output Handling
paraphrase: Downstream components act on model output without validation, enabling injection (XSS, SQL, command) or unsafe actions.
trigger: receives a flow from an llm or agent

name: Excessive Agency
paraphrase: The system grants the model more functions, permissions or autonomy than the task needs, so manipulated output causes damaging actions.

name: System Prompt Leakage
paraphrase: Instructions or secrets placed in the system prompt are exposed, and the system wrongly relies on them for security.

name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
paraphrase: Weaknesses in how embeddings are generated, stored or retrieved allow data leakage across tenants, poisoning or inversion.

name: Misinformation
paraphrase: The model produces false or misleading content that users or downstream steps rely on.

name: Unbounded Consumption
paraphrase: Uncontrolled inference requests exhaust resources or budget, degrade service or enable model extraction.
